name: Dr. Armitage
facts: Was old and white-bearded
Was one of three men from Arkham who ascended the mountain alone
Had to be helped climbing more than once
Was questioned by the group about what he knew of the thing, with no reply seeming to satisfy them
Was seen adjusting the sprayer which Rice held
Was seen chanting with the other men from Arkham, raising his arms in rhythmic incantation

sources.quote: old, white-bearded Dr. Armitage
Armitage had to be helped more than once.
Voices began questioning Armitage about what he knew of the thing, and no reply seemed quite to satisfy.
Armitage was adjusting the sprayer which Rice held, and that something must be about to happen
The chanting of the men from Arkham now became unmistakable, and Wheeler saw through the glass that they were all raising their arms in the rhythmic incantation.

name: Professor Rice
facts: Was stocky and iron-gray
Was one of three men from Arkham who ascended the mountain alone
Held the sprayer that Armitage adjusted
Had an excellent chance of spreading the potent powder over the entity from a vantage point above and behind it

sources.quote: stocky, iron-gray Professor Rice
He saw that Rice, from the party's point of vantage above and behind the entity, had an excellent chance of spreading the potent powder with marvelous effect.

name: Dr. Morgan
facts: Was lean and youngish
Was one of three men from Arkham who ascended the mountain alone

sources.quote: lean, youngish Dr. Morgan

name: Curtis Whateley
facts: Was of the undecayed branch of the Whateley family
Was holding the telescope when the Arkham party detoured from the swath
Snatched back the telescope and strained his vision to watch Rice spray the entity
Dropped the telescope with a piercing shriek into the mud after seeing an instant's flash of gray cloud

Described the entity in fragmented, panicked speech as bigger than a barn, made of squirming ropes, shaped like a giant hen's egg, with dozens of legs like hogsheads, jelly-like, with bulging eyes and many mouths or trunks like stovepipes, gray with blue or purple rings, and a half face on top
Collapsed completely after this final memory and could say no more
Was carried to the roadside by Fred Farr and Will Hutchins
fate: Collapsed and was carried away, unable to continue speaking after witnessing the entity

sources.quote: Curtis Whateley—of the undecayed branch—was holding the telescope when the Arkham party detoured radically from the swath.
Curtis Whateley snatched back the telescope and strained his vision to the utmost.
Curtis, who had held the instrument, dropped it with a piercing shriek into the ankle-deep mud of the road.

Bigger 'n a barn ... all made o' squirmin' ropes ... hull thing sort o' shaped like a hen's egg bigger'n anything, with dozens o' legs like hogsheads that haff shut up when they step ... nothin' solid abaout it—all like jelly, an' made o' sep'rit wrigglin' ropes pushed clost together ... great bulgin' eyes all over it ... ten or twenty maouths or trunks a-stickin' aout all along the sides, big as stovepipes, an' all a-tossin' an' openin' an' shuttin' ... all gray, with kinder blue or purple rings ... an' Gawd in Heaven—that haff face on top!...
This final memory, whatever it was, proved too much for poor Curtis, and he collapsed completely before he could say more.
Fred Farr and Will Hutchins carried him to the roadside and laid him on the damp grass.

name: Wesley Corey
facts: Took the telescope and reported that Armitage was adjusting the sprayer which Rice held
Cried out that something must be about to happen

sources.quote: Then Wesley Corey, who had taken the glass, cried out that Armitage was adjusting the sprayer which Rice held, and that something must be about to happen.

name: Henry Wheeler
facts: Rescued the fallen telescope and wiped it clean of mud after Curtis dropped it
Turned the rescued telescope on the mountain to see what he might
Whispered 'I guess he's sayin' the spell' as he watched a figure raising its hands rhythmically
Saw through the glass that the men from Arkham were all raising their arms in rhythmic incantation

sources.quote: only Henry Wheeler thought to rescue the fallen telescope and wipe it clean of mud
Henry Wheeler, trembling, turned the rescued telescope on the mountain to see what he might.
"I guess he's sayin' the spell," whispered Wheeler as he snatched back the telescope.
Wheeler saw through the glass that they were all raising their arms in the rhythmic incantation.

name: Fred Farr
facts: Carried the collapsed Curtis Whateley to the roadside along with Will Hutchins

name: Earl Sawyer
facts: Took the telescope and reported the three figures standing on the topmost ridge, level with the altar-stone but at a distance from it
Reported that one figure seemed to be raising its hands above its head at rhythmic intervals

sources.quote: Earl Sawyer now took the telescope and reported the three figures as standing on the topmost ridge, virtually level with the altar-stone but at a considerable distance from it.
One figure, he said, seemed to be raising its hands above its head at rhythmic intervals

name: the entity
facts: Left a swath in the grass and bushes that trembled as it moved with snail-like deliberateness up the mountain
Was being pursued by three men from Arkham
Was invisible until sprayed with a potent powder, at which point it appeared as an instant's flash of gray cloud about the size of a moderately large building

Was described by Curtis Whateley as bigger than a barn, made of squirming ropes, shaped like a giant hen's egg, with dozens of legs like hogsheads, jelly-like in substance, with great bulging eyes all over it, ten or twenty mouths or trunks along its sides big as stovepipes, gray with blue or purple rings, and a half face on top

sources.quote: the grass an' bushes is a-movin'! It's a-goin' up—slow-like—creepin' up ter the top this minute
It was one thing to chase the nameless entity, but quite another to find it.
High above the toiling group the great swath trembled as its hellish maker repassed with snail-like deliberateness.
the party were seen to gain the minor elevation only a short time after the invisible blasphemy had passed it
this sprayer was expected to give the unseen horror a moment of visibility
Those without the telescope saw only an instant's flash of gray cloud—a cloud about the size of a moderately large building—near the top of the mountain.
Bigger 'n a barn ... all made o' squirmin' ropes ... hull thing sort o' shaped like a hen's egg bigger'n anything, with dozens o' legs like hogsheads that haff shut up when they step

Had an altar-stone near its topmost ridge

name: Arkham
facts: Was the home of the three men (Armitage, Rice, and Morgan) who ascended the mountain to confront the entity
